verdict.rationale: OpenCode ships its own GitHub integration. Mentioning /opencode or /oc in a comment makes it execute tasks in a GitHub Actions runner, work in a new branch and submit a PR. Headless pieces support unattended runs: `opencode serve` runs a headless server, `opencode run` takes a one-off prompt, and `--auto` auto-approves permissions. However, these are comment-triggered or one-off actions; no recurring schedule or built-in background automation manager is documented. Missing for 10: native scheduled/recurring automations, a first-class background automation setup and monitoring experience, and hands-on corroboration of unattended runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Mention /opencode or /oc in your comment, and OpenCode will execute tasks within your GitHub Actions runner.
it will work in a new branch and submits a PR with all the changes.
The opencode serve command runs a headless HTTP server that exposes an OpenAPI endpoint that an opencode client can use.
Start OpenCode with `--auto` to automatically approve permission requests that are not explicitly denied.
